sources: ACS NTDB Annual Report 2016 (mechanism %, body region %, case fatality)
Joint Trauma System / CoERCCC Joint En Route Care Guidelines FY26 (TCCC-aligned management)

Morel-Lavallée / closed degloving case literature (Eplasty, PMC4364262)

inspect: massive bleeding from groin/axilla — no room for a tourniquet
very bloody scalp wound — looks worse than it is, but CAN cause shock if ignored
palpate: check for step-off underneath (depressed skull fracture)

inspect: partial or complete amputation; vessels may spasm and bleed less than expected at first
missing digit(s), part may be in the sawdust or the machine

injuries.name: Ring avulsion (ring degloving)
injuries.classes: Urbaniak I: circulation intact · II: inadequate circulation · III: complete degloving/amputation

inspect: skin and soft tissue stripped off the finger like a glove; bone/tendon exposed (class III)
patient: 'I jumped off the truck and my ring caught'

inspect: skin + subcutaneous fat torn off muscle in a flap or sleeve; dirt/road debris embedded

injuries.name: Closed degloving (Morel-Lavallée lesion)

inspect: skin intact but bruised, abraded or friction-burned over the hip
palpate: soft fluctuant 'water balloon' feel; skin moves over the underlying tissue

injuries.teachingPoint: The skin looks fine. The hematoma underneath can hold liters.

inspect: large part of the scalp torn off at the galea; heavy bleeding
large abraded areas with embedded gravel; can be full-thickness like a burn

injuries.name: High-pressure injection injury (paint/grease gun)

inspect: tiny pinhole wound on the finger — looks trivial
patient: 'just a little poke from the paint sprayer'

injuries.teachingPoint: A pinhole that looks like nothing: high amputation risk without surgery within hours.

scene: is the dog still loose? SCENE SAFETY first

history_card: 'I punched a guy in the mouth' — may lie at first

injuries.name: Impaled object (rebar, knife, branch)
exceptions: remove only if it obstructs the airway or prevents CPR

inspect: mangled, grass- and soil-contaminated wound; partial amputation possible
mangled hand, partial digit amputations, burns, powder tattooing
exit wound may be larger/irregular — or absent (retained bullet)

injuries.name: GSW chest

inspect: wound to the chest; check the back (log roll) for exit

spawns: requires: wound in 'the box' (between nipples, clavicles to costal margin)

inspect: entry wound; abdomen may be distending

injuries.name: GSW head

inspect: entrance/exit wound, possible brain matter (gore setting)

injuries.outcomeRealism: frequently non-survivable; triage implications in MCI

inspect: bowel protruding through the wound (gore setting)

auscultate: absent breath sounds on the affected side

injuries.name: Open pneumothorax (sucking chest wound)
spawns: higher if non-vented seal not burped

monitor: hypotension, narrow pulse pressure, electrical alternans, PEA
findings._note: Beck's triad present in a minority of cases

injuries.name: Rib fractures (elderly)
injuries.teachingPoint: Each rib fracture raises mortality in older adults; pain control prevents pneumonia.

injuries.name: Commotio cordis
mechanisms: baseball/hockey puck/lacrosse ball to the chest

scene: young athlete collapsed after being hit in the chest

injuries.teachingPoint: Survival depends almost entirely on time to defibrillation.

injuries.name: Blunt aortic injury
injuries.outcomeRealism: most die on scene; survivors are a 'contained' tear

patient: left shoulder pain (Kehr's sign) in splenic injury

inspect: seatbelt sign across the lower abdomen

injuries.name: Pelvic fracture (open-book / lateral compression / vertical shear)

palpate: DO NOT rock or spring the pelvis — gentle palpation once at most

injuries.name: Open fracture
injuries.grades: Gustilo I–III (wound size, contamination, vascular injury)

inspect: bone through skin or wound over a fracture

patient: can't bear weight; may have been on the floor for hours

inspect: leg SHORTENED, INTERNALLY rotated, flexed and adducted

injuries.name: Calcaneus fracture (fall landing on feet)
injuries.teachingPoint: Heels broken from a fall: check the spine — axial load travels up.

patient: pain out of proportion; pain on passive stretch

scene: limb pinned under a heavy object > ~1 h

inspect: purple face/neck, petechiae, subconjunctival hemorrhage above the compression line

patient: LUCID INTERVAL: knocked out, wakes up and talks normally, then crashes

monitor: Cushing's triad: bradycardia, hypertension with wide pulse pressure, irregular respirations

scene: alkali (drain cleaner, cement) worse than acid

injuries.name: Ruptured eardrum
injuries.teachingPoint: Marker of blast exposure — look for blast lung and bowel injury.

effects.skin: WARM, dry, pink below the injury

inspect: singed nasal hair, soot in mouth, carbonaceous sputum
small entry/exit wounds hiding massive deep tissue damage

injuries.name: Trauma-induced hypothermia

effects.coreTemp: falls with exposure, wet clothing, cold fluids, cold blood (TUNE)

injuries.teachingPoint: Hypothermia happens even in Florida summer. It's part of every major trauma.

summary: Hip pain, often with pelvic fracture.
Stridor, voice change; early definitive airway/cric.
Blood at the meatus; no Foley (CC).
Decreased breath sounds; can progress to tension under positive pressure.
Hyperkalemia, dark urine, renal failure; fluids.
Elderly down for hours; fluids, check K+ effects on ECG.
Foot drop after posterior hip dislocation.
Deficit below the level; neurogenic shock possible.
Neck wound: occlusive dressing; left lateral/Trendelenburg; sudden collapse.
